issues.explanation: Gunshot noise is difficult to reconcile as a primary trauma-linked trigger for childhood physical abuse by a caregiver, especially when no other items suggest weapon-related or combat/shooting associations.

issues.item: Triggers: Tactile (Temperature): A specific temperature on the skin
issues.explanation: A highly specific temperature-on-skin trigger is not impossible, but with the rest of the profile it lacks a plausible link to the stated trauma and is unsupported by memory or threat content; together with gunshot noise it makes the trigger set feel clinically disconnected from caregiver physical abuse.

issues.item: Body Unreliable: I can no longer trust my own body
issues.explanation: For childhood physical abuse by a caregiver, the profile is otherwise organized around shame/self-concept and social avoidance. 'Body Unreliable' is less coherent with the rest of the selected items because there are no accompanying threat or memory items indicating prominent somatic threat, dissociation, injury-related beliefs, or body-based trauma processing. Within this formulation, Negative Appraisals is strongly linked to maladaptive avoidance and modestly linked with triggers; the other appraisals fit that pattern, but this item introduces a distinct body-failure theme that is not supported elsewhere in the profile.

vignette: Rohan, a 36-year-old detective of South Asian descent, had always prided himself on being a rock for his loved ones. But behind closed doors, he struggled with demons that haunted him since childhood. Growing up, Rohan endured physical abuse at the hands of his caregiver, an experience that left an indelible mark on his psyche. As an adult, certain triggers transported Rohan back to those dark days. The sensation of a specific temperature on his skin would send shivers down his spine, making him feel like he was reliving the trauma all over again. He couldn't quite explain why, but sleeping alone or in unfamiliar places made him anxious, too - perhaps it was the feeling of vulnerability that came with not having someone to rely on for protection. Even the sound of doors opening or slamming would startle him, as if his body was constantly on high alert. These triggers reinforced Rohan's deepest fears: that he was a lousy coper, unable to handle the stressors of life. He felt like he didn't know himself anymore - the confident detective who solved crimes with ease had given way to a fragile individual who couldn't even manage his own emotions. And beneath it all, there was a nagging sense that something was fundamentally wrong with him as a person. As Rohan's self-doubt grew, so did his maladaptive strategies for coping. He began avoiding people, including his loving wife and colleagues, in an attempt to shield himself from further emotional pain. Staying up late into the night became a habit, too - by delaying sleep, Rohan felt like he was maintaining some semblance of control over his life. And going out? That seemed like an impossible task; what if something triggered another flashback or anxiety attack? But these avoidance behaviors only served to reinforce Rohan's negative self-image. By pushing people away, he convinced himself that he was indeed unworthy of love and connection. His late-night wakefulness led to fatigue, which further eroded his confidence in his ability to cope with the demands of his job. And by staying indoors, Rohan felt like a prisoner in his own home - another reminder that something was defective about him. As time passed, Rohan's negative appraisals began to sensitize him to even more triggers. The slightest noise would send him spiraling back into memories he'd rather forget. And the cycle continued: avoidance led to feelings of inadequacy, which in turn amplified his sensitivity to those triggers that haunted him most. It wasn't until Rohan's wife staged an intervention - expressing her deep concern for his well-being and their relationship - that he realized he needed help. The thought of losing the people he loved, coupled with the toll his symptoms were taking on his job performance, finally pushed Rohan to seek therapy. As he sat in the therapist's office, he couldn't shake off the feeling that this was a last-ditch effort to reclaim his life - and himself.
